title: Risotto con Carciofi
subtitle: Artichoke and lemon risotto
excerpt: Risotto con carciofi is a spring risotto made with globe artichoke hearts cooked in lemon, white wine, and olive oil. The artichoke flavour is delicate and slightly bitter, which the Parmesan finish rounds out. It is a Venetian and Roman spring dish.
sourceNotes: Artichoke risotto is a classic of Venetian and Roman spring cooking. The artichoke (carciofo romanesco in Rome, carciofo violetto in Venice) is one of the defining vegetables of Italian spring.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Prepare the artichoke hearts up to 2 hours ahead and keep in acidulated water.

content.text: Preparing artichokes takes patience: the outer leaves must be stripped back until only the pale inner leaves and the heart remain, and the choke (the hairy centre) must be removed with a teaspoon. As each heart is prepared, drop it immediately into a bowl of water with the juice of half a lemon to prevent browning. Tinned artichoke hearts can be substituted if fresh are unavailable.

Prepare the {{globe-artichoke}} artichokes: strip outer leaves until you reach the pale inner leaves. Cut off the top third. Halve and scoop out the choke with a teaspoon. Cut each heart into thin slices. Keep in lemon water until needed.

Heat 2 tbsp of the {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the artichoke slices, season with {{salt-table}} of the salt, and cook for 8 minutes until tender and lightly golden. Set aside.

Heat the remaining oil in a heavy pan over medium heat. Cook {{onion}} onion for 8 minutes until soft. Add {{garlic}} garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add {{carnaroli-rice}} rice and stir for 2 minutes. Pour in {{white-wine-dry}} wine and stir until absorbed.
Add hot {{vegetable-stock}} stock a ladleful at a time, stirring for 18 minutes until the rice is al dente. Stir in the cooked artichokes.

Remove from the heat. Stir in {{unsalted-butter}} butter, {{parmesan}} Parmesan, and the juice of the {{lemon}} lemon. Season with remaining {{salt-table}} salt. Scatter {{parsley-flat}} parsley over and serve.

items.cause: They were exposed to air after cutting.
items.fix: Drop each prepared artichoke heart straight into cold water acidulated with lemon juice. Do not prepare them in advance without this step.

content.text: Artichoke risotto is a spring dish found from Venice to Rome. In Venice, the small violetto artichokes from Sant'Erasmo island in the lagoon are prized for their tenderness. In Rome, the large carciofo romanesco variety is used. The artichoke season in Italy runs from February to May and this risotto is one of the first signs of it.
